key_insight: A precision-first, physics-checked literature pipeline builds electro-optic datasets that support property prediction for unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: The approach could guide electro-optic material selection for optical modulators and quantum microwave-to-optical links.
method: Acquire relevant papers and extract values using layout-aware LLMs and deterministic table parsers.
Apply three-tier verification, symmetry checks, notation normalization, and provenance tracking.
Aggregate cross-paper values using median and median absolute deviation; audit a noise-robust surrogate with leave-one-material-out testing.
evidence_signal: From 49 papers, 414 of 816 candidates were accepted; exact-match precision/recall were 0.51/0.48, while held-out baseline wins rose from 1/4 to 9/13 as coverage expanded from 10 to 22 materials.
watch_item: Moderate exact-match accuracy warrants continued curation, and the uncontrolled snapshot comparison does not establish that database expansion caused prediction gains.
paper_title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
